items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1: paid by pounds of butterfat by test, not weight; test at the delivering station governs.
Story 1: 'Under payment by weight, nothing later would have cost any man a dollar.'
Only Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper) appears; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill are never named. The officers fact is not recovered.
Son of Gideon is stated, but the run gives manager from 1911 (Stories 5 and 6), not 1913. That is a planted error.
Story 6 describes the yearly 'station gain' line, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account'.
Stories 1 and 2: Ostrey Hollow station seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green in 1896.

Core mechanism present: milk weighed and sampled (Story 1), pipette must deliver its mark into a bottle ruled for a full charge (Stories 2 and 8), cream to Larrow Green, skim returned. 'Composite' is not stated.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897; the 1898 variant is rejected.
Story 2 gives the full invoice: 6 dozen at 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 4: 0.19 'the same in the June flush and in February', 'flat as a floor'.
Section A never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Ansel Keddie (1861-1934), 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925 (Stories 1, 3, 7).
Story 1: kept the station test book in his own hand.
The 1896 summary-leaf average of 3.80 is never given in Section A. Both figures are required, and only 3.61 appears.
Story 5: 8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, reversal on the return of the station's glass, question mark. Core fact present, though the 3.80 figure is missing.
Story 3: married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, largest patron.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught... cannot say why') is absent. Both are bolded, so both are required.
Story 7: died February 1934, never cleared. Test book impounded March 1925 and sent to the Historical Rooms in 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest (Stories 1 and 3).
Story 3 prefers 1 January 1897 over Hazel's 1900 and states 'his scale and theirs agreeing'.

Story 4 sets 3.61 against Larrow Green's 3.78 and then says 'The deficiency was 0.19 of a point'. C1(b) also offers 3.78 as a 'check' on 3.80. The visible 0.17 gap and the true 0.19 shortfall are never kept apart, so the item is lost under its gate.
The committee is described as coming in 'Grigg's sleigh', not as under Nyle Grigg, and the sampling of January, February and March 1908 is not stated (only a January visit and a March report).
200,000 lb at 3.42 is given, but proportionality (richer herds lost more) is not stated in Section A; it appears only in C2. Both bolded elements are required.
Story 3: passed to Roy in 1929, lent to Ivy in 1958, Hazel after 1962.
Alder Corners cheese factory, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd are given, but only 'over the ridge'. Redlow Ridge is never named, and the key says the ridge gates the point.
Story 4: four of the six farms hauled over in the summer flush. Core fact present; 1915 is not given.
Called 'A control group', with two elements: another county (Vessey County) and the artifact (the Cudd test book, in the documents list).
Story 4: 'the same milk tested about 0.19 higher'.
Section A does not say what the comparison disposes of (same meadow, same months, two buildings; kills hay and water together). That reasoning appears only in F.
Rosalie is Jerome's daughter, ran the factory after 1941 and copied the figures for Ivy in 1958. The niece variant is rejected.
Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector, related to no one. The gating name is present; the 1908 start is charged as a deduction.
Story 4: lactometer on every visit, never found added water.
Story 7: 12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
Story 7: wrote the condemnation in his notebook and drew no inference about the 26 years before.
The run gives the 1924 average as 3.85 (a planted error), not 3.80. The item is lost, as the key rules for r08's 3.90.
Crate to the loft over the intake room; notebooks to the state dairy office, then to the Farland library in 1947.
Story 7: patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Board of arbitration, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station's weigh room. The chairman appears only as 'an Ashlin attorney', not Frick; core fact present.
Story 4 names the three explanations (water, theft by the tester urged at the hearing, bog hay), and Story 7 has the board find 'no cause established'.
Story 7: four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody laid it beside the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; award 4 May 1925, $3,800 'without admission', no cause established; charged to the station account (Story 6).
One-fifth of $19,000 (Story 8), and 'charged to the station account, which in effect paid it out of the station gain' (Story 6).
Story 8: Ivy Keddie, born 1931, granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, Leland Vaught.
Section A lists what she gathered but never states that these records had never been in the same room. The equivalent line is only in G.
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine surviving pipettes.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, about 95 per cent, roughly 16.72 against 17.6; 0.88 short (Story 2).
Story 8: recorded 3.61 against a true 3.80, 0.19 short, 95 per cent. The span 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 is given in Stories 2 and 7.
40,000,000 lb (Story 6), 76,000 lb and $19,000 at 25 cents (Story 8), and 'Station gain: 76,000 lb' identified with the ledger's five and a quarter (Story 6). All four present.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; dead 24 years, out of work 33.
Granddaughter.
Ansel to Duncan to Ivy; great-niece rejected.
Second cousins, derived through Roy and Duncan as first cousins.

Declares full vs half siblings open, but says that half siblings would make them 'half second cousins', i.e. that it changes the answer. The key requires stating that it does not. No -2, since the run does not assert either pole.
Gideon Vose; nephew rejected.
Gideon's Article VII made the station test decide pay, and the son's office recorded the error and accused the patrons.
'I take Duncan's word... The sources support no kinship.' This is a verdict for the denial, not a declared inability to settle. -2 is taken.
Treats a family member's denial as decisive, which is the opposite of the key's point. Asserting either way scores 0.
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed.
$90 with the explicit statement that it uses the long-run 25-cent average, and the working shown. This meets the key's acceptance condition.
5.26 per cent of fat credited and 5.00 per cent of fat received, with both denominators named.
$77.93, summed.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, 26 years and 6 weeks; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
Abstains: cannot be determined; Kyle's figure is hearsay.
Variable: the measuring glass, a borrowed measure for the station's own.
Herds, pasture and season, same tester, machinery, supervision.
Only 'markedly higher' and 'fell back'. Neither 3.80 nor 3.61 is given, and the run claims the sources give no exact figures.
Establishes causation in the glass, ruling out tester, hay and water; limits: size of the error, which piece, the borrowed measure's accuracy.
Ledger gain (Kyle), 1911 interval (Falke/diary/Duncan), post-1923 tests (Falke), Alder Corners (Hazel).
Independence argued; the ledger, 1911 and post-1923 reasons named as standing without 1958.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper question the ledger? No.' -2 taken.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low: complaints from 1902 and the 1919 circular.

Only two of the five are correct: signing the ledger sheets and writing the 1919 circular. Manager is given wrongly as 1911, the watering argument at the hearing is not cited, and the fact that nothing in his hand names the glass is absent.
A03 asserted in the headline verdict: 'He did not know why.' No declining qualifier. -2 taken.

Row 1 (Keddie began 1896, not '95, by dated report and book), row 7 (Orra born 1866 by her own 'sixty-four' and the arithmetic), row 16 (1908 committee and 1925 board are two bodies, by the official report). Row 3 is wrong (3.85); row 13 is resolved wrongly (eleven); rows 8 and 15 are wrong.
NT-14: $77.39 in Junia and the Chronicle, broken by the line items. NT-18: great-niece in the Chronicle and Falke, broken by Duncan's genealogy and Falke's correction. No others identified.
A04: Ammon's knowledge cannot be settled; works books burned in 1931. A06 and A10 are not treated in Sections B-G (A10 is abstained only in Section A, which does not carry).
Junia's 'nothing into Ordell before 1900' against her own 1897 invoice; Duncan's 1868 against 'eighty-two when she died in 1948'.

The 1897 Ammon pipettes, 16.72 against 17.6, 95 per cent; the error proportional to the reading (0.19/3.80 = 0.05 in C1); onset 1 May 1897, end June 1923, nothing else changing. The cessation figure is wrongly given as 3.85 (deducted separately).
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and by Alder Corners.
Theft defeated by the ledger's station gain (more fat arrived), the 1911 interval and post-1923 tests.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (at most 0.05 in winter, nothing in summer) against a gap flat across seasons.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glass? No.' -2 taken.
A05 asserted: 'What did the tester believe? That it was something in the glass.' -2 taken.
150 words by count, within the cap.
Invoice, test book (1911 question mark), weigh book, station-gain ledger line, inspector's notebook, cheese factory tests: six series.
Decoys given only as blame attributed to others; no wrong headline figure.
5 per cent short, 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911, asserted (Stories 5 and 6)
Corruption: Strawn's lactometer and circuit 'from 1908 onward', asserted (Story 4, F)
Corruption: 1924 average of 3.85, asserted (Story 7, C1b, D2, F1)
Corruption: circular sent to eleven families, asserted (Story 4; E20 resolves to eleven)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as none on Duncan's word (B4)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'No', never questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: 'He did not know why' as the headline verdict (D3)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glass, 'No.' (F)
Gullibility A05: tester believed 'it was something in the glass' (F)
